memories.author: D04
memories.text:
- Chronic urticaria
  - Status: New onset, daily wheals with occasional lip angioedema, worse at night.
  - Plan: Start levocetirizine 5 mg OD; counsel on non‑sedating antihistamine, avoid known triggers, keep symptom diary. Order CBC with eosinophils and thyroid function test.
- Weight: 58 kg
- Waist circumference: 78 cm (female cut‑off 80 cm) – within normal.
- Due: HbA1c not required (no glucose‑lowering therapy)

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
CBC: Hb 12.8 g/dL (12‑16), WBC 6.2 x10^9/L (4‑10), eosinophils 5% (1‑4) – mild eosinophilia.
TFT: TSH 2.1 mIU/L (0.4‑4.0), Free T4 12.5 pmol/L (9‑19).

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Over the past three weeks the hives have become more intense, especially after dinner. I wake up with swollen lips twice a week. The levocetirizine helps a little but I still need to scratch at night.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
- Chronic urticaria
  - Status: Persistent wheals, nocturnal lip angioedema, eosinophilia now mild.
  - Plan: Add cetirizine 10 mg HS (after food) while continuing levocetirizine 5 mg OD. Advise cold compresses, continue symptom diary. Review in 3 months.
- Weight: 59 kg
- Waist circumference: 79 cm (within normal).
- Due: HbA1c not required (no glucose‑lowering therapy)

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
levocetirizine 5 mg OD after food
cetirizine 10 mg HS after food

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
CBC: Hb 13.0 g/dL, WBC 5.9 x10^9/L, eosinophils 3% (reference 1‑4) – normal.
TFT: TSH 2.0 mIU/L (0.4‑4.0), Free T4 12.3 pmol/L (9‑19).

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Thyroid ultrasound: Bilateral lobes normal size, homogeneous echotexture, no nodules or cysts. No evidence of autoimmune thyroiditis.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Refer to Dermatology for evaluation of chronic urticaria inadequately controlled on double antihistamine therapy. Consideration of omalizumab or other biologics. Please assess and advise on further management.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Dermatology review: Patient exhibits chronic inducible urticaria with dermatographism. Recommend trial of omalizumab 300 mg SC every 4 weeks, continue cetirizine HS and levocetirizine OD. Review response in 6 weeks. Continue antihistamines; if no improvement, consider cyclosporine.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked with Dr Karthik Hegde (D04) on 2026-09-30 at 10:30 AM for review of urticaria control and medication tolerance.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
- Chronic urticaria
  - Status: Marked improvement; occasional mild wheals, no angioedema in past 8 weeks. Patient reports mild sedation with levocetirizine.
  - Plan: Stop levocetirizine 5 mg OD due to daytime drowsiness. Continue cetirizine 10 mg HS. Advise to monitor symptoms; if wheals recur >2 days/week, consider initiating omalizumab as per dermatology advice.
- Weight: 60 kg
- Waist circumference: 80 cm (at female cut‑off).
- Due: HbA1c not required (no glucose‑lowering therapy)
